data.name: Vaikunth
data.gender_notes: Vaikunth is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The divine, eternal and supreme abode of Lord Vishnu, where he is present in his infinite form. The name Vaikunth carries the meaning “Abode of Vishnu” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu. Parents who choose Vaikunth usually hope their child will grow to embody abode of vishnu and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name signifying the ultimate spiritual goal and the eternal abode of the divine
data.etymology: Vaikunth belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Abode of Vishnu.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vaikunth total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Vaikunth" has significant cultural significance in Hinduism, representing the ultimate spiritual goal for devotees of Lord Vishnu. It is believed that upon attaining moksha or liberation from the cycle of birth and death, the soul reaches Vaikunth, the abode of Lord Vishnu. Vaikunth is considered to be a realm of pure bliss, a transcendental paradise where all desires are fulfilled, and one is free from all worldly troubles.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, the name Vaikunth is synonymous with the concept of the Divine Presence and the ultimate goal of self-realization. It is a symbol of the infinite love, grace, and mercy of Lord Vishnu. The name is believed to have the power to bestow upon the devotees peace, happiness, and spiritual growth. By chanting the name of Vaikunth, one can purify the mind, eliminate negative emotions, and connect with the Divine Presence. The name "Vaikunth" serves as a reminder of the ultimate spiritual goal and inspires one to strive for self-realization and union with the Supreme Being.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vaikunth symbolizes the divine abode of Vishnu, a spiritual realm of eternal peace and happiness. It is the ultimate destination, a place of pure love and bliss, free from all suffering and sorrow.

historical_references.reference: Vaikuntha is the name of the heavenly abode of Vishnu, the preserver deity in Hinduism. It is described as a place of supreme bliss, where the devas (gods) live and the souls of the virtuous go after death.
historical_references.context: Puranic literature and Hindu scriptures, such as the Bhagavad Purana and the Mahabharata, describe Vaikuntha as the divine realm of Vishnu and the ultimate destination for the souls of the devout.

historical_references.reference: The name Vaikuntha is also associated with a legendary king of the same name, who ruled over the kingdom of the same name in ancient India. Vaikuntha is believed to have been a great devotee of Vishnu and is said to have attained the divine abode after his death.
historical_references.context: Hindu epics and folklore, such as the Purananuru and the Agni Purana, narrate stories of King Vaikuntha and his devotion to Vishnu, and his eventual attainment of Vaikuntha, the divine abode, after his death.

trends: Vaikunth is a popular name in Hindu mythology, often associated with the abode of the god Vishnu and the eternal paradise.
modern_usage.modern_context: In modern usage, the name 'Vaikunth' is often used in various contexts, including hashtags (#VaikunthMasala, #VaikunthJeevan) on Twitter, Instagram filters (VaikunthDham), and subreddits (r/Vaikunth). It is also referenced in Indian pop culture such as movies (Vaikunth Vijay) and TV shows (Vaikunth Omkara). The name is also used in various spiritual and religious contexts, particularly during festivals and religious events.
